chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) judged regarding a slave girl whose husband had divorced her with two divorces, then had sexual relations with her, so he had him whipped.

key_terms.وَقَعَ عَلَيْهَا: He had sexual relations with her

ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling for a slave girl who receives two divorces and her husband then has relations with her?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi illustrates the application of the 'three divorces make her unlawful' rule specifically within the context of a slave girl, where the husband's subsequent intercourse after two divorces triggers a flogging penalty. It highlights the distinct legal status of slave women in Shia jurisprudence, where the counting of divorces and the consequences of remarriage differ slightly from free women, emphasizing the Imam's role in clarifying these nuances. The ruling underscores the importance of tracking marital status changes to determine the validity of subsequent unions and associated penalties.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> judged regarding a slave girl whose husband had divorced her with two divorces, then had copulated with her, so he<sup>asws</sup> had him whipped’.
